## Conclusions
**Setup.** Same 15,905 images, recipe, seed and 310 steps as 010; only the captions differ: the COCO Captions of
those images (`scripts/build_coco_captions_set.py`, 79,319 captions, 4.99/img, 10.4 words/cap, people kept,
left/right sentences dropped because of flips) instead of LPCVC-style RefCOCO/+/g referring expressions
(4.81/img, about 5 words). Ran from `3c2fa78` plus the uncommitted `--train-file` option, committed right after as
`a1f1e61` (no other change). The train loss is about 4x lower than 010's: whole-scene captions are easy to tell
apart inside a random batch, so they give a weak training signal for fine-grained object captions.

**Results (paired, same validation images; 010 numbers from its own run):**

| | RefCOCOg-LPCVC | LPCVC sample |
|---|---|---|
| pretrained B | 71.38 | 88.91 |
| FT on COCO Captions (020) | 75.69 (+4.31 [+3.2, +5.4]) | 91.03 (+2.12) |
| FT on RefCOCO/+/g (010) | 87.34 (+15.96) | 91.37 (+2.46) |
| 020 − 010 | **−11.65 [−13.3, −10.1]** | −0.34 [−1.8, +0.9] (n.s.) |

**What we learned.**
1. On validation, COCO Captions recover only 27% of the fine-tuning gain. Switching from the proposal's COCO
   Captions to RefCOCO-family captions is justified on our validation set, and by a wide margin.
2. **Caveat, stated plainly:** validation is RefCOCOg-derived, so it favors RefCOCO-family training by construction
   (013 already showed +13.0 without any RefCOCOg caption, which rules out a pure RefCOCOg-leak explanation, but not a
   "RefCOCO style" one). On the LPCVC sample, the only set outside the RefCOCO family, both caption types give
   about the same gain (+2.1 vs +2.5); the difference is not significant, and 56 images cannot resolve it. So the sample
   supports "fine-tuning on objects in COCO images helps", not specifically "RefCOCO captions are better".
3. Both fine-tunes are still ahead of the pretrained model on the sample, which agrees with 014 (+2.16 [+0.4, +4.2]).

**Decision.** Keep RefCOCO-family captions as the training data (better or equal everywhere we can measure), and say
in the report that the size of the validation gain overstates the LPCVC gain. The held-out test fold
(`scripts/build_test_set.py`) is also RefCOCO-family, so it carries the same caveat. A non-RefCOCO, LPCVC-like
check (category-clustered, attribute captions) is the next soundness item. The checkpoint is local only
(`checkpoints/020_ft-b-cococaptions/`, an ablation, not uploaded to Drive).
